objective: Audit generic optimizer policies for forecast/reforecast, transversal candidate generation, alternative-plan switching and crash-safe evaluation when progress overruns expectations.

observations.claim_scope: Hyperband allocates a predefined resource across many configurations and uses adaptive resource allocation/early stopping rather than fully evaluating every configuration. This supports a probe-then-intensify control pattern, not a general proof that any early metric predicts final utility.

Ray Tune documents ASHA as terminating less-promising trials and allocating more resources to promising trials. Its restore API resumes unfinished trials from persisted experiment state/checkpoints, while SIGKILL can skip a graceful final checkpoint. This is checkpoint-based recovery, not exactly-once protection for arbitrary external evaluator side effects.

For runtime minimization, SMAC3 can abort a challenger once cumulative cost cannot beat the incumbent. This gives a concrete fail-fast rule based on an irreversible lower bound on accumulated positive runtime cost.

SATzilla uses empirical hardness/runtime models for per-instance solver selection and historically falls back to the next predicted solver on solver failure. This supports explicit alternative ranking and forecast-conditioned switching, but its published setting is solver selection rather than long-horizon self-improvement.

Hydra iteratively adds configurations to the extent that they improve a current portfolio, rewarding complementary strengths rather than merely local variants of the incumbent. This is a useful analogue for transversal candidate generation.

observations.mechanism: universal restarts under unknown runtime distributions
observations.claim_scope: For Las Vegas algorithms with independent restarts, the universal restart strategy is within a logarithmic factor of the best restart strategy without knowing the runtime distribution. This only transfers when repeated attempts are meaningfully independent and restart-safe.

observations.mechanism: persistent study state and stale-trial detection
observations.claim_scope: Optuna documents heartbeat-based detection of killed/hung RUNNING trials with RDBStorage and optional retry; JournalStorage lacks heartbeat and can leave a parameter combination blocked. Retry is operational recovery, not evidence that an external side effect can be safely repeated.

candidate_control_policies.name: direct-first conditional reforecast
candidate_control_policies.rule: Start with the cheapest credible direct plan. At fixed durable checkpoints, condition the forecast on the fact that the plan is still unfinished: estimate P(complete before deadline | elapsed=t, unfinished) and expected remaining cost, rather than comparing elapsed time with a static full-run percentile. Continue only while conservative current utility remains competitive with the best alternative after switch cost and uncertainty margin.
candidate_control_policies.reason: A static p90 trigger can be later than the remaining deadline under heavy-tailed runtimes; conditional survival information is more decision-relevant after an overrun.

candidate_control_policies.name: transversal generation and race
candidate_control_policies.rule: When overrun or forecast-calibration alarms fire, generate a small set of candidates from deliberately different mechanism families, score marginal portfolio value on the incumbent's failure set, allocate equal probe budgets, then intensify only survivors with successive-halving/adaptive-capping style resource allocation.
candidate_control_policies.reason: Local variants can share the incumbent's failure mode; portfolio complementarity is the target, not merely raw standalone score.

candidate_control_policies.name: utility-advantage switching
candidate_control_policies.rule: For plan i at checkpoint t, define U_i(t)=P_i(success within remaining budget)-lambda*E_i(capped remaining cost)/(remaining budget)-risk_penalty_i. Switch only when a conservative alternative estimate exceeds the current estimate by switch_cost_normalized plus hysteresis, or when the current plan is forecast-infeasible before the deadline.
candidate_control_policies.reason: This prevents universal fixed timeouts from harming easy/direct-good regimes while still permitting early abandonment in heavy-tail/decomposition-favorable regimes.

candidate_control_policies.name: Luby restart safety fallback
candidate_control_policies.rule: If runtime calibration is poor, runtimes appear heavy-tailed, and reruns are independent plus side-effect-safe, fall back to a universal restart schedule rather than relying on a misspecified point forecast. Do not use this fallback for deterministic progress, non-independent reruns, or non-idempotent external effects.
candidate_control_policies.reason: Unknown heavy-tail regimes can make a single long attempt arbitrarily unattractive, but restart theory assumes safe independent reruns.

candidate_control_policies.name: crash-safe evaluation envelope
candidate_control_policies.rule: Before an expensive or externally visible evaluation, persist a stable attempt/candidate identity and evaluation intent. On restart, reconcile an in-flight attempt before any retry. If provider semantics prove neither idempotent same-key replay nor reconciliation, persist UNKNOWN and fail closed rather than blind-retry. Derive selection evidence only from immutable completed outcomes.
candidate_control_policies.reason: Checkpoint/retry frameworks recover computation but do not automatically make external evaluator effects exactly once.

forecast_metrics: deadline success calibration: compare predicted P(success by B) with observed frequency in held-out history
runtime calibration: p50/p90 coverage plus median absolute log runtime error on completed runs
conditional calibration after overrun: for each checkpoint t, compare predicted and observed remaining-time survival among runs unfinished at t
forecast drift: rolling calibration error relative to the model snapshot used when the plan was chosen
candidate_triggers_for_calibration_not_u: soft reforecast whenever elapsed exceeds the initial median forecast or a new blocker changes plan state
generate transversal alternatives when elapsed/initial_expected_time >= 1.5, branch-count/forecast >= 1.5, or deadline-success forecast falls below a precommitted floor
switch only after two consecutive checkpoints of alternative utility advantage unless the current plan is already deadline-infeasible
use a hysteresis margin so small noisy score changes do not cause thrashing
cap a challenger immediately when accumulated positive cost proves it cannot beat the incumbent under the active objective
no_regression_restoration_metadata: baseline artifact/state digest and immutable restore pointer
forecast model snapshot, calibration window and uncertainty summary used for the decision
budget consumed before switch, switch checkpoint, reason code and alternative ranking
immutable outcome/evidence log cursor used by the decision
best-safe incumbent pointer plus explicit rollback preconditions

synthetic_ablation.purpose: Stress-test decision rules only; not external empirical evidence.

regimes.direct_good: direct median~8 light-tail; decomposition ~15; transversal median~14
regimes.direct_heavy: direct 70% median~8 / 30% median~50 mixture; decomposition ~15; transversal median~18
regimes.decomp_good: direct 50% median~10 / 50% median~70 mixture; decomposition ~14; transversal median~22

bounded_inference: A universal fixed timeout can waste work in a direct-good regime.
A static p90-overrun trigger can be unusable in heavy-tail regimes because the calibrated p90 can lie beyond the entire deadline.
A conditional reforecast rule can preserve the direct-good case while switching in the two heavy-tail regimes in this synthetic setup.
The numerical lambda, hysteresis and checkpoint schedule are candidate settings only; they require calibration on non-synthetic workloads before adoption.

crash_safe_evaluation_local_evidence.scope: Own clean-state sequence 101 demonstrated a local HTTP/SIGKILL reference in which stable idempotency plus reconciliation recovered provider-accepted/local-unrecorded effects without duplicate execute, while a provider with neither capability failed closed as UNKNOWN. This is reused only as a generic crash-safety invariant, not as evidence about arbitrary providers.
